subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable memory recall eligibility and index exclusion paths for markdown-first workspaces

question: Should OpenClaw add configurable include/exclude path scopes for built-in Memory Search indexing and memory-core short-term recall eligibility, and where should that config live?
rationale: This is a new compatibility-sensitive config surface spanning plugin-owned memory behavior and shared memory indexing, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add shared memory path scopes
options.body: Introduce one shared include/exclude evaluator used by memorySearch indexing and memory-core recall eligibility, with defaults preserving current behavior and tests covering diagnostics and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Narrow to memorySearch exclusion first
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95739 or a successor as the first step and leave recall eligibility/include scopes for a separate accepted design.

options.title: Defer to memory plugin convergence
options.body: Leave the request open until memory plugin convergence can define the path-scope contract alongside broader memory architecture decisions.

recommendation.title: Add shared memory path scopes
recommendation.body: Introduce one shared include/exclude evaluator used by memorySearch indexing and memory-core recall eligibility, with defaults preserving current behavior and tests covering diagnostics and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The request is closest to recent memory host SDK and memory/QMD configuration work and needs a decision about the exposed config/API shape.
